principles: Motion must reveal, compare, focus, explain, or transition; decorative movement alone is not a reason to animate.
Prefer one dominant moving focal region at a time so the viewer always knows where to look.
Do not run perpetual particles, floating dots, random decorative lines, jitter, or attention-stealing loops on information scenes.
Prefer restrained mask/clip reveals, opacity, position and scale, data-driven chart growth, and sparse camera-like depth over gimmicky bounce or overshoot.
Use one transition language per video; vary intensity by narrative importance, not randomly by scene.
A newer model or workflow may raise this profile, but should not silently lower the minimum score floor.

upgrade_rule: Bump version whenever the quality floor, required review checks, or motion language materially changes; old release receipts must then be re-reviewed before publishing.
